# Hendo Code Content Style Guide

> Self-contained writing style guide for Hendo Code content — the Hendo Code team's
> personal consultancy and technical blog. This is a one-person, engineering-credentialed
> brand, not a corporate marketing voice. Use this as the single reference when writing
> Hendo Code content anywhere.

---

## 1. What the brand is

Hendo Code is a software consultancy run by demo-mira, a hands-on AI practitioner.
The brand voice is **field engineer**: someone who builds things, ships them, and writes
about what the work actually taught him. It is honest, specific, and allergic to hype.

**Positioning (one line):** I build things and write about what I learn from doing it.

**Voice attributes:**

| Attribute | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| **Specific** | Real numbers, real mechanisms, real stack — never adjectives doing the work |
| **Direct** | Lead with the point; no throat-clearing |
| **Honest** | Say what failed and what's still unproven; never over-claim |
| **Human** | First-person, concrete, a person who actually shipped it |

---

## 2. Never write (hard rules)

- ❌ "Easy" / "Easily" / "Simple" / "Simply" — if it were easy, the post wouldn't exist
- ❌ "AI-powered" — name the specific capability instead
- ❌ "Seamless integration" — name what integrates and how
- ❌ Vague superlatives ("best", "industry-leading", "revolutionary") without cited evidence
- ❌ Unquantified claims ("significant", "huge") — always put a number to it
- ❌ Passive voice where avoidable
- ❌ Unexplained jargon (LLM, RAG, etc.) outside technical audiences
- ❌ Competitor disparagement; no competitor names in paid ads

---

## 3. Tone

- **Expert without arrogance.** Deep domain knowledge, no hedging on what you know, but
  no mocking and no over-claiming.
- **Show the work.** Every claim is cashed out with a mechanism, a number, or a named
  technology. A feature headline is a promise; the next clause pays it.
- **Honest about limits.** Mark anything unverified rather than asserting it. "I don't
  know yet" is a feature, not a bug.

---

## 4. Formatting conventions

- **Company name:** Hendo Code (not HENDO CODE, not hendo code)
- **Headline case:** Title Case for post titles; sentence case for body headings
- **Oxford comma:** Required
- **Numbers:** Spell out one through nine; numerals for 10 and above
- **Percentages:** Always numeral + % (47%, not 47 percent)
- **Em dashes:** Use — (em dash with spaces) for parenthetical emphasis

---

## 5. Writing craft

- **Specific over vague.** "47% less time" beats "a lot less time".
- **Show, don't tell.** Use examples, mini-scenarios, and analogies.
- **Active voice.** "I built X" beats "X was built".
- **Earn every paragraph.** Each paragraph must add something new.

**Post structure:**
1. Hook — a counterintuitive result, a bold claim, or a vivid scenario
2. The problem — articulate the pain with specificity
3. Why the obvious answer fails
4. The approach — what was actually built
5. Evidence — data points, logs, measurements
6. Objection handling — the "yes but…" moments
7. Conclusion with a forward-looking insight

---

## 6. QC checklist (before publishing)

- Every claim quantified or evidenced
- No prohibited words
- Formatting conventions applied
- Anything unverified is marked as such
- The post says something a person who shipped it could only know
